m.x: An elastic ease-in, where the value oscillates back and forth with a spring-like motion beforeaccelerating toward the target. The effect begins with a series of small oscillations thatgrow in magnitude, simulating a stretched elastic band being released. Use this when you wanta tween to feel springy or bouncy at its start before snapping into motion.

p.x: The value to be eased, between 0 and 1.
The amplitude of the elastic oscillation. Values below 1 are clamped to 1. Higher values produce a wider oscillation arc.
Controls how tight the sine-wave oscillation is. Smaller values produce tighter, more frequent cycles; larger values produce wider, slower oscillations.

m.x: An Elastic ease-in/out, combining both the ease-in and ease-out elastic effects.This easing function produces a spring-like oscillation at both the start and endof the tween, overshooting the target value before settling. It is useful foranimations that need a bouncy, elastic feel at both ends of the transition.

p.x: The value to be eased, typically in the range [0, 1].
The amplitude of the elastic oscillation. Values below 1 are clamped to 1.
Controls how tight the sine-wave oscillation is. Smaller values produce tighter waves with more cycles.

m.x: An Elastic ease-out, where the value overshoots its target and oscillates with a decaying sine wavebefore settling at the final value. The elastic effect occurs at the end of the transition, makingthe motion appear to bounce or spring into place. Accepts a normalized input value `v` in the range 0 to 1.

p.x: The normalized value to be tweened, typically in the range [0, 1].
The amplitude of the elastic overshoot. Values above 1 increase the size of the overshoot.
Controls how tight the sine-wave oscillation is. Smaller values produce tighter waves with more rapid oscillations.
